subtype_info: spontaneous subdural haematoma secondary to dengue fever
title: Imaging of the neurological manifestations of dengue: A case series
case_text:
A 55-year-old male presented with a 1-day history of left hand and right leg weakness, slurred speech, occipital headache and giddiness. He also had a single episode of convulsions. He reported intermittent high-grade fever with chills five days prior to presentation and was subsequently diagnosed with dengue fever with a platelet count of 75 000/microl. The patient was normotensive with no recent trauma or bleeding from any site.
MRI of the brain revealed a well-defined crescent-shaped extra-axial collection overlying the right cerebral convexity which appeared iso to hyperintense on T1-weighted and FLAIR images and of mixed signal intensity on T2-weighted images (Figure 6a-f). The collection demonstrated blooming on GRE images, suggestive of an acute to subacute subdural haematoma (Figures 6g and 6h).
A diagnosis of spontaneous subdural haematoma secondary to dengue virus fever was made.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Dengue
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: spontaneous subdural haematoma secondary to dengue fever
